questions.cardText:
[Archaeology] What was the earliest known purpose of Sumerian writing?
A. Recording religious texts
B. Accounting and administrative records
C. Writing laws
Answer: B. Initially, writing in Sumerian civilization was solely for accounting purposes until about 3000 BCE. As time progressed, their focus on the afterlife may have facilitated the emergence of literature, as shown in the use of writing for inscriptions on tombs and other funerary artifacts.
questions.de: Wozu diente die sumerische Schrift (Protokeilschrift), die aus tönernen Zählsteinen hervorging, ursprünglich?
questions.en: What was the earliest known purpose of Sumerian writing (proto-cuneiform), which grew out of clay accounting tokens?

timeline.labelEn: Proto-cuneiform, the earliest Sumerian writing, emerges in Mesopotamia (c. 3350–3200 BC)
timeline.labelDe: Die Protokeilschrift, die früheste sumerische Schrift, entsteht in Mesopotamien (um 3350–3200 v. Chr.)

questions.notes: Confirmed: proto-cuneiform arose from the token-based accounting system and recorded administrative operations. The card's explanation (an afterlife focus leading to tomb inscriptions) reads more like ancient Egypt than Sumer and is not supported by the source.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] Where is chocolate originally from?
A. Indonesia B. Belgium C. Mexico
Answer: C. Chocolate has its origins in ancient Mesoamerica, present-day Mexico, where the Maya and Aztec civilizations first made chocolate from cacao seeds.
questions.de: In welcher antiken Kulturregion mit dem Zentrum im heutigen Mexiko tranken Kulturen wie die Olmeken, Maya und Azteken Kakaogetränke, von denen eines, die Schokolade, im 16. Jahrhundert nach Europa gelangte?
questions.en: In which ancient cultural region, centred on present-day Mexico, did civilizations such as the Olmecs, Maya and Aztecs drink cacao beverages, one of which, chocolate, reached Europe in the 16th century?

timeline.labelEn: Chocolate, a Mesoamerican cacao beverage, is introduced to Europe in the 16th century
timeline.labelDe: Schokolade, ein mesoamerikanisches Kakaogetränk, gelangt im 16. Jahrhundert nach Europa

questions.notes: Card's answer (Mexico/Mesoamerica) is fine for chocolate as a drink, but the cacao tree was first used and domesticated earlier in South America (present-day southeast Ecuador, Mayo-Chinchipe culture, c. 5,300 years ago) before reaching Mesoamerica; the question therefore asks about the Mesoamerican cacao drinks. The 'Engineering and Inventions' discipline is the card's own.
